$comment: Ceilings for every shipped wasm artifact, read by `cargo xtask size` against the cargo artifact `cargo xtask dist wasm` ships (the release build with remapped paths, before wasm-bindgen and wasm-opt). Shrink-only: a ceiling more than the headroom above its artifact fails until lowered with `cargo xtask size --update`; raising one is a hand edit, and its reason says why the growth is worth it.

whiteboard-wasm.reason: Production exports only, measured at the cargo artifact: 2500331 bytes, the shipped (wasm-bindgen stripped) module 1584844. Raised by hand from 2485000 to 2502000 for comment layers (ADR-0054 step 7, S15g; owner decision q73, as at S15b): the request carries threads, commentLayer, showResolved and commentObstacles, so layout_spatial_canvas answers a board carrying threads instead of the request gate skipping it, 16950 bytes of the cargo artifact and 8233 of the shipped module above S15j's 2483381 and 1576611. Measured before S15j merged (against S15f's 2478646): the composer's comment layer was already linked, since building with the request read but the composer handed no threads saved 16 bytes; the thread reader was 10426 bytes, measured by building without it, and the rest the obstacles reader, the comment caps and the options reaching the composer. At S15j, 2483381 and 1576611, raised by hand from 2481000 to 2485000 for the font handle (ADR-0054 step 7, S15j; owner decisions q76 and q73): register_layout_fonts parses a measurer's faces once into an instance-held registry and answers a handle, release_layout_fonts forgets it, and layout_spatial_canvas names its font-table measurer by that handle instead of taking the faces' bytes as a second argument, 4735 bytes of the cargo artifact and 2497 of the shipped module above S15f's 2478646 and 1574114 (the registry, its caps, which charge each face's family name beside the bytes, and the faces reader, which the request reader used to hold). It took one daemon layout from about 1.4 ms to 0.3 ms over the vendored faces, the copy of 1.45 MB it no longer makes. Before that, 2478646 and 1574114, raised by hand from 2464000 to 2481000 for themes (ADR-0054 step 7, S15f; owner decision q73, as at S15b): the request carries a style and the families the surface holds, so layout_spatial_canvas answers the document style and a theme id instead of the request gate skipping them, 16847 bytes of the cargo artifact and 12729 of the shipped module above S15d's 2461799 and 1561385. Measured before S15d merged (against S15i's 2422995): the theme-drawing paths were already linked (pinning every request to the clean style saved 53 bytes); about 13 KB is the reader of the plugin's themes.json into token bundles (theme::tokens), measured by building with an empty theme table, and the rest the request's two fields. The reader is total, the shape being the registry's to judge, because one that refused field by field cost 5.8 KB more in drop paths; the families are a list searched in order, as the expansion ids are, since a sorted set cost 15.6 KB. Before that, 2461799 and 1561385, raised by hand from 2425000 for fence tokens as data (ADR-0054 step 7, S15d; owner decisions q75 and q73): 38804 and 16608 bytes above S15i's 2422995 and 1544777. Measured per function off the name section before the merges, the same growth was 16821 bytes of code (the highlighter gate, the codeTokens reader, the tokens table and the set of fences asked for, and the highlighted-run path the typesetter now reaches) and 27424 of name section the shipped module strips; building the tokens table with inserts instead of collect saved 6.3 KB of bulk-build sort. At S15i, 2422995 and 1544777, raised by hand from 2423000 to 2425000 for the per-node expansion policy (ADR-0054 step 7, S15i; owner decision q73, as at S15b): the request carries the ids of the file nodes drawn open, which let layout_spatial_canvas answer a board whose file nodes expand unevenly instead of skipping it, 1948 bytes of the cargo artifact and 821 of the shipped module above S15b's 2421047 and 1543956. That left 5 bytes under the old ceiling, below the minimum headroom, so the ceiling moves to keep it. The ids are a list searched in order, since a sorted set cost the cargo artifact 18997 bytes. Before that, 2421047 and 1543956 after a raise by hand from 2415000 for the shortcode tables (ADR-0054 step 7, S15b; owner decision q73: accept the growth, raise per slice, keeping the minimum headroom): from 2374709 (shipped 1500181) the cargo artifact grew 46338 bytes and the shipped module 43775, of which 40168 is the emoji table itself (packages/plugin-visual/src/emoji/emoji-shortcodes.tsv, 1914 slug and character rows, embedded as text) and the rest the two candidate scans and the icon-name lookup, which let layout_spatial_canvas answer a body holding shortcodes instead of declining it. Before that, 2374709 and 1500181 after the reference host learned to narrow a canvas embed to its fragment (ADR-0054 step 7, S15e: select_canvas_fragment, 8188 and 3783 bytes above the 2366521 and 1496398 measured at S15c, within the ceiling); at S15c after the font measurer lost its segment cuts and their joining table (ADR-0054 step 7, S15c: 1850 and 1415 bytes below the 2368371 and 1497813 measured at S14b). Raised by hand for layout_spatial_canvas (ADR-0054 step 7, S14b), the whole layout in one call, as owner decision q70 anticipated: from 1270280 (shipped 787954) the cargo artifact grew 1098091 bytes and the shipped module 709859. Of that, the markdown parser and the mdast conversion (whiteboard-markdown behind whiteboard-codec::parse_markdown_body, linked for the first time) are 329809 of the cargo artifact and 252655 of the shipped module, measured by building with the body parse stubbed out; the rest, 768282 and 457204, is whiteboard-canvas-render entering the artifact for the first time: the composer, the typesetter, line breaking with its generated table, the BudouX model, the theme layer, the font-table measurer and its sfnt reader, the scene writer and the reference host. What else the artifact carries is unchanged: abi_version, edge_route_layout over the router, anchor pass, repair, crossing sweep and side-choice search, the OKF codec behind okf_parse and okf_serialize, the JSON Canvas codec behind json_canvas_parse and json_canvas_serialize, and facet_bucket_check. The per-module layer-2 test exports (the det_* batches, edge_route_on_grid, and each edge module's edge_* export) stay behind the `oracle-surface` cargo feature. Every released build ships this artifact (the npm tarball, the Docker image and the web site); the whole layout's switch defaults to `ts`, so only `differential` and `rust` call it.
